title: Set Up New Outlook for Windows
cardText: Set up Microsoft 365, Outlook.com, Gmail, IMAP and supported POP email accounts in new Outlook.
Configure email accounts, authentication and provider mail settings.
Synchronise IMAP or Exchange mail, and safely transfer local POP or PST messages when required.
text: This guide covers setting up email accounts in new Outlook for Windows.
Identify the email provider and account type before starting.
IMAP and Exchange normally restore server-stored mail and folders automatically after account configuration.
Check for local-only folders, PST archives and other data that will not be restored by server synchronisation.
For an existing POP mailbox, protect locally stored messages before changing computers or email clients.
When local mail must be imported, use a separate staging folder and check for duplicates before merging.
New Outlook and classic Outlook have different settings and data file capabilities.

identifySetupType.title: Identify the email setup
body: Determine whether this is a new account setup or a migration from an existing email application.
For migrations, identify whether the existing account uses POP, IMAP or Exchange.
IMAP and Exchange generally synchronise server-stored mail and folders.
POP messages may exist only on the original computer.
For a new account without existing mail, proceed directly to account configuration.

checkOldMailStorage.title: Identify where the existing mail is stored
body: Check the original email application's account settings.
Determine whether the account uses POP, IMAP or Exchange.
IMAP and Exchange normally store synchronised messages on the provider's server.
POP accounts may contain downloaded messages that no longer exist on the server.
Classic Outlook commonly stores POP messages in a PST file.
Check for separate local-only folders, PST archives or other stored mail regardless of the account type.
Do not remove the original account until important local data has been protected.

link.name: Microsoft: Outlook PST and OST Files
link.description: Explains Outlook data files and locally stored mail.

backupPopMail.title: Back up existing POP email
body: On the original computer, open classic Outlook if that was the previous email client.
Select File, Account Settings, Account Settings.
Open the Data Files tab.
Identify the PST file associated with the existing POP account.
Select Open File Location to locate the file in Windows.
Close Outlook before copying the PST.
Copy the PST to a separate, reliable backup location.
Check for additional PST archives containing older messages.
Preserve Inbox, Sent Items, custom folders, contacts and other locally stored data.
If the old client is not Outlook, use its supported export or backup procedure.
Verify the backup before changing the original account.

link.name: Microsoft: Export Outlook Mail to PST
link.description: Official instructions for exporting Outlook data.

backupPopMail.alt: Classic Outlook Account Settings showing the Data Files tab and Open File Location button
backupPopMail.caption: Use classic Outlook's Data Files tab to locate existing POP mail archives.

backupExistingMail.title: Protect existing IMAP or Exchange data
body: Compare the original mailbox with the provider's webmail service where available.
Check that important messages and folders are stored on the server.
Identify any local-only folders, PST archives or exported messages.
Back up local data that will not be restored by normal server synchronisation.
Check contacts and calendars separately because IMAP itself does not synchronise them.
Keep the original email installation available until the new setup has been verified.
Do not export the entire server mailbox unnecessarily if all required mail is already synchronised.

protectOriginalMail.title: Protect the original email data
body: Important existing messages or local data have not yet been backed up.
Locate the original mail files or use the source application's export facility.
Check POP messages, Sent Items, archives, contacts and local folders.
Keep an untouched backup of required local data.
Do not delete the previous email configuration until the backup has been verified.
Resume the setup after protecting the mail.

identifyAccountProtocol.title: Identify the email account type
body: Determine whether the account belongs to Microsoft 365, Outlook.com, Gmail, Yahoo, iCloud or another email provider.
Check whether the provider supports automatic setup in new Outlook.
For third-party hosting, obtain the recommended IMAP, POP and SMTP settings.
Prefer IMAP when mail must synchronise across several devices.
POP may be needed for an existing workflow but does not synchronise local mailbox folders between devices.
Check the installed new Outlook version's support for the required account type.
Use the provider's supported modern authentication method.

link.name: Microsoft: Add an Email Account to Outlook
Microsoft: New Outlook Feature Comparison
link.description: Current new Outlook account and feature support.

collectMailSettings.title: Collect incoming and outgoing mail settings
body: Obtain the email address and username required by the provider.
Record whether the incoming connection uses IMAP or POP.
Record the incoming server hostname, port and encryption.
Record the outgoing SMTP hostname, port and encryption.
Common IMAP settings use port 993 with SSL/TLS.
Common POP settings use port 995 with SSL/TLS.
Common SMTP settings use port 587 with STARTTLS or 465 with implicit TLS.
These are examples; confirm the actual settings with the provider.
Check whether OAuth, multifactor authentication or an app-specific password is required.
Confirm that new Outlook supports the provider's required configuration.

obtainProviderSettings.title: Obtain the correct provider settings
body: The required incoming, outgoing or authentication settings are unavailable.
Check the email provider's official setup documentation.
Confirm the server names, ports, encryption and authentication method.
Check whether the account can be configured in new Outlook.
Do not guess server addresses or disable encryption to force a connection.
Continue when the correct settings are available.

addEmailAccount.title: Add the email account to new Outlook
body: Open new Outlook for Windows.
Select Settings or open View, View settings.
Navigate to Accounts, Your accounts or Email accounts depending on the installed version.
Select Add Account.
Enter the email address and select Continue.
Complete the provider's sign-in and verification process.
For Microsoft 365 and supported providers, Outlook normally detects the settings automatically.
If supported manual configuration is required, enter the provider's documented settings.
Complete setup and check that the account appears in Outlook.

link.name: Microsoft: Add Email Account in New Outlook
link.description: Official procedure for adding an account.

addEmailAccount.alt: New Outlook for Windows showing the Add Account dialog
addEmailAccount.caption: Open account settings, select Add Account and enter the email address.

troubleshootAccountSetup.title: Diagnose account setup failure
body: Record the exact error displayed during account setup.
Check whether the provider supports new Outlook and the selected email protocol.
Verify incoming, outgoing and encryption settings.
Check whether multifactor authentication, OAuth or an app password is required.
For managed Microsoft 365 accounts, check organisational client access restrictions.
If the necessary POP or manual configuration options are unavailable, consider classic Outlook or Thunderbird.
Avoid repeatedly attempting incorrect credentials.

testEmailConnection.title: Test incoming and outgoing email
body: Check that the account appears in new Outlook.
Send a test message to another accessible email address.
Reply from that address and confirm the response arrives.
Check that the outgoing message appears in Sent Items.
Check for authentication, delivery or synchronisation errors.
Once sending and receiving work, identify whether this is an IMAP or Exchange mailbox or a POP-based setup.
IMAP and Exchange mail should be checked for normal server synchronisation before considering any import.

troubleshootMailFlow.title: Investigate sending or receiving failures
body: Determine whether incoming mail, outgoing mail or both are failing.
Compare Outlook with the provider's webmail service.
Check authentication errors, server rejections and synchronisation failures.
For manually configured accounts, verify the provider's server settings.
Check mailbox storage and account restrictions.
Use the Email Not Working guide for more detailed diagnosis.

checkAccountSyncType.title: Does the account synchronise its mailbox?
body: Identify the configured account type in Outlook.
Microsoft 365, Exchange, Outlook.com and IMAP accounts normally synchronise server-stored messages and folders.
A POP account may contain messages that exist only in local storage.
For IMAP or Exchange, check server synchronisation first rather than importing the old mailbox.
For POP, check whether messages must be recovered from an existing PST or another local archive.

verifyServerSyncedMail.title: Verify IMAP or Exchange synchronisation
body: Allow Outlook to finish synchronising the mailbox.
Compare Outlook with the provider's webmail service where available.
Check Inbox, Sent Items, Drafts, Archive and custom server folders.
Open a selection of older messages to confirm they are available.
Some folders may require expanding the account or allowing additional time to synchronise.
Compare server-stored message dates and folder contents rather than importing a PST immediately.
If the expected messages are present in webmail but missing in Outlook, investigate the synchronisation problem.
If the server-stored mail is correct, continue to check for local-only data.

investigateSyncMissing.title: Investigate missing synchronised mail
body: Determine whether the missing messages exist in webmail.
If they are in webmail, investigate Outlook synchronisation, account connection, folder visibility and any active filters.
Check the correct account and folder, including Archive and Deleted Items.
Allow enough time for larger mailboxes to synchronise.
If the messages are absent from webmail but present in the old application, determine whether they were stored in a local-only folder or archive.
Do not import the entire old PST until the source and location of the missing messages are understood.
Correct the issue or identify the local data that must be migrated.

checkMissingMailSource.title: Is the missing mail stored locally?
body: Check whether the missing messages are available in the original email application but absent from webmail.
Look for local folders, separate PST archives or messages downloaded by a previous POP configuration.
If the messages are local-only, preserve the source files before attempting a transfer.
If the messages are not present locally or on the server, importing an unrelated archive will not correct the problem.
Investigate the account, provider or backups when the missing data cannot be located.

checkLocalOnlyData.title: Check for local-only folders or archives
body: After confirming normal IMAP or Exchange synchronisation, inspect the original email application.
Check for separate PST archives, locally stored folders and messages not visible in webmail.
Check local Sent Items, older archives and any mail previously downloaded by POP.
Contacts, calendars, signatures and rules may also require separate migration depending on where they were stored.
Do not import the old mailbox if every required message is already synchronised.
If local-only mail exists, ensure it has been backed up before transferring it.

confirmLocalBackup.title: Confirm local mail is backed up
body: Locate the local-only messages or archive on the original computer.
For classic Outlook, identify the PST using File, Account Settings, Account Settings, Data Files.
For another application, use its supported export or backup method.
Keep an untouched copy of the source archive.
Verify that the backup contains the required folders and messages.
Do not start an import until the local-only data is protected.

link.name: Microsoft: Export Outlook Data to PST
link.description: Official instructions for preserving locally stored Outlook mail.

checkMailMigration.title: Check whether POP or local mail needs importing
body: Determine whether old messages or folders must be transferred from another computer or email application.
For an existing POP setup, check the original PST or local mail archive.
Compare the old archive with messages available in the newly configured account.
A new POP setup does not automatically restore messages previously removed from the server.
Check older Inbox messages, Sent Items and locally created folders.
If the required mail is already available, do not perform an unnecessary import.
If local mail is missing from the new setup, ensure the original data is backed up and continue with migration.

identifyImportFormat.title: Identify the original mail file
body: Check whether the required local-only mail is stored in an Outlook PST or another application's archive.
Classic Outlook commonly uses PST files for POP messages and local archives.
An OST is a synchronisation cache and should not be treated as a PST backup.
Thunderbird and Apple Mail may use MBOX or other application-specific formats.
Preserve the original data before attempting conversion.
Determine which import method supports the source format.

link.name: Microsoft: Outlook Data Files
link.description: Information about PST and OST files.

checkPstImportSupport.title: Check PST import support in new Outlook
body: Open new Outlook Settings and navigate to Data files, Import.
Look for Outlook Data File (.pst) and its Get started option.
Microsoft documents PST import in supported new Outlook installations.
Availability and eligibility may vary by version, account type and subscription.
Check that importing into the intended destination mailbox is supported.
If the feature is unavailable, use classic Outlook or another compatible migration method.
Do not assume that opening a PST archive and importing its contents are the same operation.

link.name: Microsoft: Import Email from PST
link.description: Official PST import instructions and requirements.

checkExistingMailbox.title: Check the destination for existing messages
body: Compare the source mail archive with the destination mailbox before importing.
Check Inbox, Sent Items, Archive and custom folders.
Look for overlap between old POP messages and mail already present on the server.
Compare sample messages using sender, recipient, subject, date, contents and attachments.
Check the destination mailbox's available storage.
Do not import directly into an existing Inbox or Sent Items when overlapping messages may exist.
Use a separate staging location where the chosen import method supports it.

prepareImportFolder.title: Prepare a separate mail import folder
body: Prepare a staging folder such as Imported Old Mail.
For IMAP or Exchange, use a folder under the destination mailbox when the import method supports it.
For a POP-only destination, consider retaining the old PST as a separate archive instead of merging it into the active mailbox.
Avoid choosing an existing Inbox, Sent Items or Archive folder as the destination for an uncontrolled import.
Check whether source subfolders will be retained beneath the staging folder.
Keep the source archive unchanged.
If the import tool cannot target an appropriate separate folder, use a compatible alternative rather than risking an uncontrolled merge.
A separate folder isolates the imported messages but does not automatically remove duplicates.

link.name: Microsoft: PST Import and Destination Folders

selectImportMethod.title: Select the supported mail import method
body: Use new Outlook's PST importer only if its import feature and destination are supported.
If new Outlook cannot import the PST, use classic Outlook to open it and copy selected messages into a separate folder.
For MBOX, EML or another format, use a compatible client or supported conversion workflow.
Use the prepared staging location rather than merging directly into existing mailbox folders.
If the old data only needs to remain accessible as an archive, importing it into the live mailbox may not be necessary.
Do not import the same archive repeatedly without checking the previous transfer.

importPstMail.title: Import PST messages into a separate folder
body: Keep an untouched backup of the original PST.
Open Settings, Data files, Import in new Outlook.
Under Outlook Data File (.pst), select Get started and Select file.
Browse to the PST and open it.
Select the source folder and include subfolders where required.
Review any available duplicate-handling options.
If a Do not import duplicates option is available, it may reduce overlap but is not a guaranteed deduplication method.
Under Choose a destination folder, select the correct mailbox.
Create or select a separate Imported Old Mail folder where supported.
Avoid importing directly into Inbox or Sent Items.
Start the import and allow it to complete.
Monitor mailbox storage and synchronisation.
Do not repeat a partial import before checking which messages were transferred.
Preserve the source PST until the final result has been verified.

link.name: Microsoft: Import PST Files into Outlook

importPstMail.alt: New Outlook Settings showing the PST import section
importPstMail.caption: Use Data files, Import and select a separate destination folder when supported.

useClassicOutlookMigration.title: Use classic Outlook or a compatible email client
body: Use a compatible classic Outlook installation if new Outlook cannot import the PST.
Keep a verified backup of the original archive.
In classic Outlook, open the PST as a separate archive using File, Open & Export, Open Outlook Data File.
Copy required messages into a separate staging folder in the destination IMAP or Exchange mailbox.
Alternatively, use classic Outlook's Import/Export wizard where the destination and duplicate handling can be controlled safely.
For MBOX or EML sources, use a compatible client such as Thunderbird to import the messages locally first.
Copy required messages into a separate destination folder in manageable batches.
Allow server synchronisation to complete.
Check webmail for messages intended to be stored on the server.
Do not repeat an import without checking what was already transferred.

link.name: Microsoft: PST Import in Classic Outlook
Mozilla: Thunderbird Mail Import
link.description: Official import options for other mail formats.

checkPartialImport.title: Check a failed or incomplete import
body: Do not immediately repeat the entire import.
Inspect the staging folder and identify messages already transferred.
Check for mailbox storage limits, connection failures, unsupported items or damaged archives.
Compare the completed folders and message date ranges with the original source.
Correct the identified problem before another attempt.
If another transfer is needed, use a new clearly labelled staging folder or select only missing messages.
Retain the original archive and partial import until the result is reconciled.

reviewImportedMail.title: Compare imported mail with existing messages
body: Open the Imported Old Mail staging folder or the separately retained archive.
Compare its messages with the existing Inbox, Sent Items, Archive and relevant custom folders.
Look for duplicates using sender, recipient, subject, date, contents and attachments.
Messages in the same conversation may have identical subjects but still be different messages.
Confirm that older local-only or POP messages missing from the server are present.
Check important attachments and subfolders.
Do not bulk-delete messages based only on matching subjects or dates.
Decide whether the imported mail should remain separate or be selectively merged.

resolveImportDuplicates.title: Resolve duplicates or missing imported mail
body: Compare suspected duplicates against the existing destination messages.
Check message contents and attachments before treating messages as duplicates.
Remove confirmed redundant copies from the staging area only after verifying that the required message exists elsewhere.
If messages are missing, inspect other source folders or the original archive.
For large archives, review smaller batches.
Keep the untouched original backup.
If the imported messages cannot be reconciled safely, leave them separate rather than merging.

chooseMailDestination.title: Keep the archive separate or merge reviewed mail
body: Decide whether the imported messages should remain in Imported Old Mail or another separate archive.
A separate historical archive can be sufficient for old POP mail.
If normal mailbox placement is required, transfer only messages confirmed to be missing from the destination.
Prefer copying reviewed messages rather than moving them until the results have been verified.
Do not copy an entire unreviewed archive into an existing Inbox or Sent Items folder.
Retain the original source backup regardless of the chosen destination.

mergeImportedMail.title: Merge only the missing messages
body: Identify which messages from the staging folder are not already present in the destination.
Copy only those messages into the appropriate Inbox, Sent Items, Archive or custom folders.
Work in manageable batches.
Check copied messages and attachments in the destination.
For IMAP or Exchange, allow synchronisation to complete.
Verify the server-side copies through webmail where appropriate.
Do not remove the staging folder or original archive until the merge is confirmed.

verifyMigratedMail.title: Verify imported messages and folders
body: Compare the final mailbox or separate archive with the original source.
Check Inbox, Sent Items, Archive, Imported Old Mail and important custom folders.
Verify that required older POP or local-only messages are present.
Check sample message dates, contents and attachments.
Look for duplicates after any merge.
For IMAP or Exchange, check webmail to confirm intended server-side messages are present.
For POP or a separate PST archive, confirm that historical mail remains accessible.
Check the destination storage capacity.
Retain the original mail backup until migration has been verified.

migrationEscalation.title: Further mail migration required
body: Required mail could not be located, imported or reconciled safely.
Preserve the original PST or other mail archive.
Keep partially imported messages separate.
Record the source format, destination account, migration method and any errors.
Check for archive damage, unsupported formats, mailbox limits or incomplete synchronisation.
Before trying again, identify which messages have already been transferred.
Do not merge uncertain message sets or delete the original source.

link.name: Microsoft: Fix PST Import Problems
link.description: Official troubleshooting for PST import errors.

setupComplete.title: New Outlook setup complete
body: The email account has been configured successfully.
Incoming and outgoing messages work as expected.
For IMAP or Exchange, required server-stored messages and folders have synchronised.
If there was no missing local-only data, no mail import was necessary.
For POP or local archives, any required old mail has been transferred or retained as a verified separate archive.
Imported mail was checked for duplicates before being merged into existing folders.
Check contacts, calendars and signatures separately when required.
Retain original mail archives and backups for future recovery.

setupEscalation.title: Further new Outlook setup diagnostics
body: New Outlook cannot connect to the mailbox after checking its account settings.
Record the email provider, account type, Outlook version and exact error.
Confirm the selected protocol and authentication method are supported.
For managed accounts, check organisational security and client access policies.
If required manual settings are unsupported, consider classic Outlook or Thunderbird.
Preserve any existing POP, PST or local-only data while investigating.
